policy_title: Introduce British Jobs Bonus and Address Mineworkers' Pension
stated: Labour will introduce a 'British Jobs Bonus', allocating up to £500 million per year from 2026, to incentivise clean energy firms offering good jobs, terms and conditions, and building supply chains in industrial heartlands. The party will also address the injustice of the Mineworkers' Pension Scheme by reviewing surplus arrangements and transferring the Investment Reserve Fund back to members.

source.quote: We will reward clean energy developers with a British Jobs Bonus, allocating up to £500 million per year from 2026, to incentivise firms who offer good jobs, terms and conditions and build their manufacturing supply chains in our industrial heartlands, coastal areas, and energy communities. Labour will end the injustice of the Mineworkers' Pension Scheme. We will review the unfair surplus arrangements and transfer the Investment Reserve Fund back to members, so that the mineworkers who powered our country receive a fairer pension.

bearing_set.reason: The British Jobs Bonus explicitly incentivises 'good jobs, terms and conditions' in clean energy and supply chains in industrial heartlands, directly bearing on job quality, pay, and employment in specific regions.
The Mineworkers' Pension Scheme component would transfer the Investment Reserve Fund back to members and review surplus arrangements, directly affecting retirement income adequacy for former miners.

The bonus is directed specifically at clean energy firms; accelerating their UK supply chains plausibly increases domestic clean energy capacity and supports the emissions trajectory — a concrete mechanism beyond generic industrial subsidy.

Building clean energy supply chains in 'industrial heartlands' targets regional economic opportunity, business investment and productivity in historically low-opportunity areas — the aggregate/opportunity-side indicator of O13.

Targeting industrial heartlands explicitly addresses regional inequality (a listed O14 indicator), and correcting the mineworkers' pension surplus injustice narrows the fair-shares gap for a specific low-income worker cohort.

membership_note: Two-component policy: the British Jobs Bonus bears on job quality (O4), clean energy supply chains (O6), regional economic opportunity (O13), and regional inequality (O14); the Mineworkers' Pension component bears on retirement security (O8) and fair shares (O14).
